notes:
Summary:
- Outcome: Closed-lost to Together (primary) and Fireworks evaluated for on-prem. Replicate considered for experimentation only.
- High level: Cobalt wanted a private deployment with strict KMS + audit controls; they ran a 3-week POC with Redwood Dedicated and a parallel POC with Together.

Timeline (bullets):
- 2024-09-12: Opportunity created (initial inbound product demo). AE: Maya Chen. SE assigned: Daniel.
- 2024-09-25: Technical deep-dive with infra team (FF call ff_20241007_8741). Asked for kms/HSM attestation and data residency details.
- 2024-10-10: POC kickoff — Redwood provided dedicated pool + private control plane config. SE helped baseline throughput.
- 2024-11-04: Security questionnaire returned (lots of follow-ups). Procurement requested ISO/SOC artifacts and an on-prem packaging option.
- 2024-11-20: POC results: Redwood median p95 latency competitive but Together showed slightly lower tail latency under their workload and offered an appliance container for on-prem.
- 2024-12-10: Procurement paused due to company-wide budget freeze (Q4 hiring/contract moratorium).
- 2025-01-15: Procurement revived; vendor selection call — procurement favored Together based on committed discount, local datacenter presence, and appliance story. Internal ML infra champion had left (no internal sponsor).
- 2025-01-22: Deal closed-lost. Follow-up notes added to Drive and ticketed internal playbook updates.

POC notes / technical takeaways:
- Workload: high-throughput reranking + embeddings for personalization; target 50k qps embeddings at 20k concurrent sessions for chat.
- Redwood POC: steady-state throughput met SLA, prefix caching helped cost, but customer flagged needing HSM attestation and vendor-hosted appliance for offline audits.
- Competitor angle: Together offered aggressive committed pricing and an appliance/containerized on-prem package; Fireworks pitched lower friction for air-gapped install.

Customer quotes (paraphrased):
- "We like Redwood's runtime and the observability — great stuff — but procurement is nervous about the audit attestation and wants the on-prem appliance route."
- "Pricing commitment and local datacenter presence were deciding factors."

Next steps / churn prevention:
- Mark as closed-lost, set cadence to re-engage in Q4 2025 when budget cycles reopen.
- Action: Create internal playbook 'lost-to-together-jan2025' documenting objections (appliance ask, HSM proof, aggressive committed discounts) and standard rebuttals.
- Follow-up items for product/Security: consider a pre-packaged appliance story or clearer HSM attestation docs; capture TCO comparison template used by procurement.

Short fragments (CRM style):
- no champ -> top reason.
- procurement loved committed pricing.
- security worried about HSM attestation.
- AE: maintain contact w/ Lina (CSM) for expansion if they return.
